claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
A portion of Hf should be replaced with Ti.
Hf-to-Ti substitution is expected to alter the alloy microstructure.
The altered microstructure may produce a more favorable balance of strength and ductility.
Ti enhances solid-solution strengthening in high-entropy alloys.
Ti can improve ductility in high-entropy alloys.
Ti-mediated strengthening and ductility improvement may maintain mechanical properties while reducing density.
Replacing Hf with Ti will reduce density below 10.21 g cm−3.
The modified alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will have yield strength at or above 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Mechanical performance is to be evaluated under tensile loading at approximately 25 °C and 1000 °C.
The amount of Ti substitution required to meet the targets is unknown and must be optimized experimentally.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and uncertainty fields imply that some optimized Ti-substitution level may satisfy the targets, whereas the falsification rule says failure of any member of the composition series falsifies the hypothesis. A poorly chosen substitution level could therefore trigger rejection even if another level succeeds.
The predicted room-temperature outcome requires yield strength above 1600 MPa, while the boundary only prohibits values below 1600 MPa and therefore permits equality.
